first_in_archive: He Was A Friend Of Mine

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Cited as an example of traditional music's influence on the band [5]
- **In The Pines** (1 review): Reviewer says it evokes being among pine trees along the Eleven Point river in January [7]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 other source): Runs about nine and a quarter minutes, opening this recording [3]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (1 other source): Runs just over ten minutes, the longest track listed, and is followed by It's All Over Now Baby Blue [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Standing On The Corner**: rare: 6 archived performances [17]
- **In The Pines**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]
- **Cardboard Cowboy**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [17]
- **Cream Puff War**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- **Pain In My Heart**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]
- **You Don't Have To Ask**: rare: 7 archived performances [17]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Big Boss Man, Nobody's Fault But Mine, He Was A Friend Of Mine, Don't Ease Me In [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.21063.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 101 min; rated 4.69/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has a bubblegum, Haight-Ashbury-documentary feel; reviewer wishes Jerry were higher in the mix; Vocals are panned left in the mix, with the music on a separate track [8][10]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.89555.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 101 min; rated 4.09/5 by 22 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds pristine for its age of nearly 43 years [12]
- **gd1966-07-16.13958.serafin-marmar-sbefix-4459.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 44 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.serafin.4459.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 44 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [4]

## Around the show

- The band was introduced as the oldest juveniles in California [10]
- Reviewer hears a resemblance to the band's first album, but live, with much longer tunes [9]
- Reviewer ranks it above other 1966 shows, with 11/19/66 the closest rival, thanks to sound and scope [12]
- The 7/16 show was long for its time, compared with the shorter performance the next night [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.21063.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.miller.89555.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD [2]
- **gd1966-07-16.13958.serafin-marmar-sbefix-4459.flac16**: transferred by sbefix etc of source by Marmar; source: SBD > RTR > PCM > SSSB [3]. Also: Files were corrected with shntool for sector boundary errors and stripped of extra AIFF data; FLAC encoding by Mr. Marmar, December 2002 [3]
- **gd1966-07-16.sbd.serafin.4459.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by John "Jay" Serafin; source: SBD > RTR [4]
